dedupe_keys.name: machine learning methods for the optimisation of urban mobility

description: The implemented model infers passenger origins and destinations from fare-collection records and optimizes a bus-route network using a genetic algorithm and real road geometry. Its Lisbon application reports a four-minute reduction in average passenger travel time and increased satisfied demand. These are optimized scenario outcomes, not verified changes to operated services. This thesis has a different author and result from the later busOpt multiobjective study and is retained as a distinct documented model. The metadata do not supply a verified code repository or exhaustive optimization settings. Coverage is limited to the source-described systems and experiments. The related Zenodo deposit provides descriptive metadata, with restricted document or data access and licence label not stated. Document rights do not establish software rights or access to the underlying observations. Only full descriptive metadata, file inventories and the project metadata catalogue were reviewed; no underlying measurements, code, paper or model archive was opened.
